lead_headline: Restaurant tracker quiets to 1 new lead (41 total active) while foreclosure filings slide to 30—fourth straight week of decline from late-February peak

restaurant.blurb: 1 new lead today holds the active roster steady at 41 total (20 openings, 21 closures/temp closures). Sole Friday detection: Ogo Korean BBQ & Sushi Pronto launches counter-service concept at Union Station, helmed by chef Jackie Cho. Week's broader portfolio spans downtown density—Mendocino Farms (Union Station sandwich shop), G-Que Barbeque and C Burger both at McGregor Square, Convivio Café (Guatemalan-inspired Alliance Center spot). Closure ledger weighted toward legacy exits: Aspen Baking Company abruptly shutters March 6 after 30+ years, leaving wholesale clients scrambling; 303 Ramen suffers attic fire March 3; Colfax and Cream folds two locations after rapid expansion. Seven-day split: 20 opening leads versus 21 closures—near-parity after prior week's 2:1 attrition skew.

foreclosure.blurb: 30 new filings this week extends the four-week deceleration pattern—down 9% from last week's 33, now 39% below late-February's 49-filing peak. 39 auctions queue for next seven days, total exposure $11.2M. Lone $2M+ property surfaces: Arapahoe County's South Columbine Circle at $2.24M, followed by Weld's Falcon Drive ($618K). Weld County leads active caseload at 391, El Paso follows at 375—exurban concentration persists while Denver metro holds at 55. Four-week slide from 49→33→30 now mirrors March 2025's seasonal softening, suggesting spring auction surge stalling or displaced into April. Week-over-week filing decline minimal but directionally consistent—velocity downshift holds.

reputation.blurb: 4 mentions yesterday pull the 7-day total to 42 across 12 sources—up 14% from prior week's 37, sustaining elevated baseline three weeks post-launch. Denver Post still dominates at 38% share (16 citations), Instagram and Facebook combine for 10 social pickups. Thursday notables: Speer ghost lot market listing via Hoodline, Bitcoin lawsuit coverage across Post, cryptocurrency investor feud echoing through social channels. Google News RSS captures 41 of 42 detections. Three-week trajectory now clear: explosive Week 1 launch spike (5→53) settled into 48-mention Week 2 plateau, now Week 3 tracking 42—stabilization at ~6 daily mentions signals sustainable earned media velocity, not viral decay. Denver Post partnership driving consistent referral traffic.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 yesterday (1 new, 0 canceled) marks third consecutive single-digit day, pushing MTD to +17 (+1.3/day) with 90-day cumulative at +80. Past fourteen days reveal momentum fade: explosive March 2 opener (+4 net) and March 9 surge (+6 net) now decelerated to +1 daily crawl across Thursday-Friday. Seven-day total of +15 (23 new, 8 canceled) outpaces prior week's anemic +2, but driven entirely by early-week 6-net spike March 9—subsequent five days average +1.8/day. Cancellation floor stabilized at 1-2/day, but new subscriber acquisition cooled from mid-week 8-add peak to current 1/day trickle. March's 1.3/day rate edges above YTD's 1.2/day benchmark, but weekend must deliver to prevent late-month velocity collapse. Pattern suggests strong month-open followed by mid-month plateau—Q1 finish trajectory uncertain.
